effects: Deploys a new Safe proxy with CREATE2 that points to `_singleton`. Its address comes from the factory, keccak256(initializer) and saltNonce.

Calls the new proxy with `initializer` (normally Safe.setup). This sets the owners, threshold, fallback handler and an optional setup delegatecall (to, data) for the new Safe. It can also pay `payment` of `paymentToken` from the new Safe to `paymentReceiver`, or to tx.origin (the signer) when the receiver is zero.
The function is not payable and moves none of the signer's tokens or ETH. The signer's allowances are not spent and nothing is approved.
formats.shown: "Create Safe" with the singleton address and the decoded setup: owners, threshold, fallback handler, payment, payment receiver and the setup data. The salt is hidden.

findings.title: createProxyWithNonce: nested setup screen shows the setup data but not the delegatecall target `to`.
findings.evidence: Case 0, nested 'Account setup' fields: Signer x3, Threshold, Fallback handler, Payment, Payment receiver, 'Module' = '0x'. setup(address[],uint256,address to,bytes data,...) delegatecalls `to` with `data` from the new Safe, and no field shows `to` (zero in this case). The rendering comes from the Safe singleton descriptor that calleePath `_singleton` resolves to.
findings.fix: In the Safe singleton's setup format, add `to` as an addressName field such as 'Setup delegatecall target', next to the data field.

findings.title: createProxyWithNonce: a zero payment receiver is shown as 0x000… although Safe.setup pays tx.origin then.
findings.evidence: Case 0 nested field 'Payment receiver' = 0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000. In Safe.handlePayment, receiver = paymentReceiver == address(0) ? tx.origin : paymentReceiver.
findings.fix: In the singleton descriptor, use senderAddress [0x000…0] on paymentReceiver so the zero address is shown as the signer.

findings.title: createProxyWithNonce: the address of the new Safe is not shown because it is computed with CREATE2.
findings.evidence: SafeProxyFactory.createProxyWithNonce: salt = keccak256(abi.encodePacked(keccak256(initializer), saltNonce)); deployProxy uses create2. The descriptor has no field for the resulting address, and saltNonce is visible: never.
findings.fix: No descriptor change can derive a CREATE2 address. Wallets could compute it themselves.

findings.title: createProxyWithNonce: the singleton is shown as a raw address in the test screen, so the signer cannot tell it is an official Safe.
findings.evidence: Case 0 field 'Safe singleton' = 0xFf51A5898e281Db6DfC7855790607438dF2ca44b, with format addressName and types [contract]. Any contract can be the singleton, and it then controls the new account.
findings.fix: Rely on wallet name resolution, or add `sources` so known Safe singletons resolve to their names.

effects: Deploys a new Safe proxy with CREATE2 that points to `_singleton`, through createProxyWithNonce, and emits ProxyCreationL2.

The function is not payable and moves none of the signer's assets. No allowance is spent or granted.

findings.title: createProxyWithNonceL2: nested setup screen shows the setup data but not the delegatecall target `to`.

findings.title: createProxyWithNonceL2: a zero payment receiver is shown as 0x000… although Safe.setup pays tx.origin then.

findings.title: createProxyWithNonceL2: the address of the new Safe is not shown because it is computed with CREATE2.
findings.evidence: SafeProxyFactory.createProxyWithNonceL2 calls createProxyWithNonce, whose salt depends on keccak256(initializer) and saltNonce (visible: never). The descriptor has no field for the resulting address.
findings.fix: No descriptor change can derive a CREATE2 address.

findings.title: createProxyWithNonceL2: the singleton is shown as a raw address in the test screen.
findings.evidence: Case 1 field 'Safe singleton' = 0xEdd160fEBBD92E350D4D398fb636302fccd67C7e, with addressName and types [contract]. The singleton decides how the new account behaves.
findings.fix: Add `sources` or rely on wallet name resolution for the known Safe L2 singletons.
